title: 6 Highspot alternatives in 2026, now that Seismic owns it
summary: Highspot merged with Seismic in August 2026. Compare Highspot alternatives like GetAccept, Showpad, and Mindtickle, sorted by what you used Highspot for.
body_markdown:
Highspot isn't Highspot anymore. On August 18, 2026, Seismic completed its acquisition, and the product now operates under the Seismic name. If you signed with Highspot, you signed with a company that no longer exists as an independent business.


Staying is still a fine choice - Highspot works well for plenty of teams, and is still one of the market leaders. But if your renewal is coming up, or adoption was already a struggle, it's worth a minute to see what else is out there.


We're on this list too, so we're not pretending to be neutral. GetAccept is an AI Digital Sales Room, built for running the buyer-facing side of the deal, not content management. We're often compared to Highspot, so we'll tell you exactly where we help and where we don’t, same as every other tool here.


[Try GetAccept's Digital Sales Room for Free](https://app.getaccept.com/signup)

## Why teams are evaluating Highspot alternatives right now


First, the merger itself


.[Gartner's read](https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/7440262) on the deal: it's a defensive consolidation against pricing pressure and AI competition, and buyers should expect less negotiating leverage and slower feature releases while the two roadmaps merge.


If you're renewing this year, get commitments in writing about what happens to your specific modules and support tier. Favor a shorter term over locking in multi-year right now.


Second, the recurring problems some teams are experiencing


. Talking to teams that have come to us from Highspot and reading public reviews, a few reasons keep coming up:


- **Adoption is a recurring complaint.** For teams without a dedicated[sales enablement](https://www.getaccept.com/learning-hubs/sales-enablement) manager or RevOps support, the ramp-up can feel disproportionate to the value they get in the early months. Reps might not use it the way it was set up to be used, and admins end up reteaching the same workflows every quarter.


- **Deal room and content setup takes too long, and the room functionality is limited.** Highspot is primarily a seller-side tool, so the buyer-side functionality gets less attention.


Building a shareable space for one specific deal can eat an hour when it should take minutes. The deal room functionality is also limited.


- **Integration depth varies a lot by CRM.** Teams on HubSpot report weaker sync than teams on Salesforce, and end up paying for features they don't use as a result.


## How we evaluated


We used the same criteria across all Highspot competitors: what job it replaces, CRM integration depth, what the AI capability does, whether it's built for internal enablement or external buyer engagement, and pricing model.

Setup and day-to-day use feel less manual than what they had before. AI drafts business cases and follow-ups from actual meeting transcripts and deal context, not generic prompts.

## 2. Showpad


Best for


: Mid-market B2B sales teams that want content and coaching balanced evenly without going full enterprise.


Showpad is a sales enablement platform that combines content management, sales coaching, and buyer engagement tools into one workspace


.


It bundles content management, coaching, buyer engagement, and analytics . Genie AI handles content recommendations by deal stage, Roleplay AI lets reps practice against an AI counterpart, and Field Meeting AI captures notes from in-person conversations and updates CRM fields automatically.


### Key features


-


Centralized content management for organizing, tagging, and distributing sales assets to reps across the team


-


Sales coaching and training tools to support rep readiness and consistent messaging


-


Buyer engagement features that allow sellers to share content with prospects and track how it's consumed


-


Content analytics to understand which materials are being used and driving results


-


Integrations with major CRM platforms to connect content usage to pipeline data


### What it offers over Highspot


Showpad combines content management and sales coaching in a single platform, reducing the need for separate tools. The buyer-facing sharing capabilities give prospects a more organized experience than raw email attachments.


### Pros


-


Combines content management and sales coaching in a single platform


-


Buyer-facing sharing capabilities give prospects a more organized experience


-


Designed for revenue teams, so the use cases are more sales-specific than a general knowledge management tool


### Cons


-


Like Highspot, Showpad is primarily a seller-side and content-organization tool - deal-level buyer engagement visibility is limited compared to purpose-built Digital Sales Room platforms


-


Pricing is not publicly listed, which makes it harder to evaluate fit without going through a sales process


-


Mobile experience is strong, but admins report a setup learning curve similar to Highspot's.


### G2 rating


[4.6/5 (1,909 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/showpad/reviews?source=search)

## 3. Mindtickle


Best for


: Teams whose Highspot frustration centered on rep readiness and onboarding speed, not content findability.


Mindtickle is a revenue enablement platform built around the idea that rep readiness is the foundation of sales performance. It gives frontline managers structured workflows for coaching, skills development, and onboarding - with analytics that help leaders understand where reps need support.


If Highspot's training capabilities feel thin for what your team needs, Mindtickle goes significantly deeper on that dimension.


### Key features


-


Sales training and onboarding workflows for ramping new reps quickly and consistently


-


Coaching and skills development tools that give frontline managers structured ways to assess and develop their team


-


Content and enablement capabilities that support customer-facing selling activities


-


Analytics to track rep engagement with training programs and measure learning progress over time


-


Customer-facing enablement features for sales and success organizations


### What it offers over Highspot


Mindtickle's coaching and readiness workflows go well beyond what most content-focused enablement platforms offer. The analytics help revenue leaders understand rep skill gaps, not just content usage.


### Pros


-


Deep coaching and readiness workflows that go well beyond what most content-focused enablement platforms offer


-


Strong analytics for revenue leaders who want to understand rep skill gaps, not just content usage


-


Built for both sales and customer success teams, making it useful across the full revenue organization


### Cons


-


Primarily focused on the seller side - deal-level buyer engagement and Digital Sales Room capabilities are not Mindtickle's core strength


-


If content governance at scale is the primary need, this isn't built to be your content system of record


### G2 rating

### Pricing

-


Analytics to track content usage, coaching activity, and rep engagement with training programs

Allego combines content, learning, and coaching in one suite. The video-based practice workflows give managers a structured way to develop reps before they're in front of buyers.

## 5. Guru


Best for


: Teams that want fast content findability without a multi-week rollout. Setup can be live in a day, versus the weeks typically needed for Highspot, Seismic, or Mindtickle.


Guru takes a different angle from most tools on this list. Rather than focusing on sales content or rep coaching, it's an AI-powered knowledge management platform built for teams that need fast, reliable answers during customer conversations.


Think internal wikis, FAQs, and playbooks - surfaced in context, right where your team is already working. If Highspot feels like overkill for what is essentially a knowledge organization problem, Guru is worth a look.


### Key features


-


Centralized knowledge base for storing FAQs, playbooks, and internal documentation in a single, searchable location


-


Contextual knowledge delivery via browser extension and workflow integrations so answers surface where teams already work


-


AI-assisted search and answer retrieval that helps customer-facing teams find accurate information quickly


-


Verification and content governance tools to flag outdated content and keep the knowledge base current


### What it offers over Highspot


Guru solves a different problem - fast, reliable knowledge access for customer-facing teams. The browser-based and workflow-friendly delivery means knowledge is available in context, not buried in a separate platform.


### Pros


-


Makes knowledge easy to capture and access, especially for teams that need fast answers during customer conversations


-


Helps centralize information and reduce time spent searching across scattered docs


-


Browser-based and workflow-friendly delivery means knowledge is available in context


### Cons


-


Maintaining content quality and keeping knowledge up to date requires ongoing admin effort


-


Large or complex knowledge bases can become harder to organize over time


-


Compared with sales enablement tools like Highspot, Guru is less focused on content coaching, deal-level analytics, and enablement-specific reporting

****

Paperflite's core identity is content management, sales engagement, and content intelligence, narrower than the full suites above but sharper if that's specifically your gap.


### Key features

-


Content tracking and analytics to see how prospects engage with shared materials - opens, time spent, and activity

Sales enablement workflows designed for revenue teams managing collateral and buyer-facing content


-


Content discovery so reps can find and send the right asset without digging through folders

Paperflite is simpler and more focused than enterprise enablement platforms. Easier to get up and running for smaller teams than Highspot, with content tracking that gives reps visibility into how buyers interact with shared materials.

Less depth in coaching, training, and rep readiness features compared to platforms like Mindtickle or Allego

## How to choose: 2-minute self-check


Check every box that's true for your team. Whichever group has the most checks is where to start.


### Full platform replacement


✔️ Manager coaching and call review matter as much as content delivery


✔️ We have budget and time for a multi-week implementation


✔️ Content governance across a large team is a top-3 requirement


3+ checked


: Mindtickle if onboarding speed is the bigger pain than content findability. Showpad if it's roughly even between the two. Allego if coaching and video are the priority and you want a lower price point than either.


### Content management only


✔️ Reps mainly used Highspot to find the right deck or one-pager, nothing more


✔️ We don't need training paths, certification, or coaching workflows


✔️ Setup speed matters more than feature depth


✔️ We'd rather not touch our stack right now if we don't have to


3+ checked


: Guru for the lightest footprint and fastest setup. Paperflite if you also need buyer-facing content tracking. Staying on the merged Seismic platform and renegotiating if migration cost outweighs the frustration.


### Buyer-facing deal execution


✔️ The actual complaint is about running the deal with the buyer, not finding content internally


✔️ Building or updating a deal room/proposal manually eats more time than it should


✔️ We want buyer-level engagement data (who's engaged, who hasn't) rather than just content performance stats


✔️ E-signature and contracts currently live in a separate tool from your content or proposal tool


3+ checked


: GetAccept. You get Deal Rooms as the buyer-facing workspace, contracts and e-signature in the same place instead of a separate tool, buyer-level engagement analytics down to the stakeholder, and two-way Salesforce and HubSpot sync so activity flows back to CRM automatically. Teams making this switch have cut sales cycles by more than half by giving buyers one place to track everything.

Highspot is a content management and sales enablement platform focused on organizing assets and training reps. GetAccept is a Digital Sales Room platform focused on deal execution - giving you real-time visibility into buyer engagement, plus proposals, contracts, and e-signatures in one place. Highspot answers "what content are we using?" GetAccept answers "what's happening in this deal right now?"


-

You don't have to rip and replace. The most common pattern we see is a split stack: keep Highspot (or Seismic) for internal content storage and sales enablement, and use GetAccept specifically for the buyer-facing motion like deal rooms, proposals, e-signature, and engagement tracking.


-


###


Just the buyer-facing parts, by design. Highspot/Seismic are built for internal content storage, versioning, and sales enablement; GetAccept is built for the live interaction between seller and buyer — deal rooms, engagement analytics, proposals, e-signature.


-


###


The most detailed data point we have is from Dealfront, who moved off Highspot/Seismic: 75% reduction in time spent exchanging information with prospects. Sales cycles dropped from 150 days to roughly 50 days in several cases.
